claim: PRISMA 2020 is the current reporting guideline for systematic reviews (Page et al., BMJ 2021;372:n71; also in PLOS Medicine and Systematic Reviews).
PRISMA-S is a 16-item reporting extension for the literature search itself (Rethlefsen et al., Systematic Reviews 2021;10:39).
PRISMA-P is a 17-item checklist for a review protocol written before the review (Moher et al., Systematic Reviews 2015;4:1).
The Cochrane Handbook is at version 6.5 (2024); rapid review guidance is separate, updated in BMJ in 2024 with 24 recommendations.
Kitchenham and Charters adapt the review method to software engineering: plan, conduct, report, with a protocol validated in advance (EBSE-2007-01).
Garousi, Felderer and Mantyla extend the guidelines to grey literature (blogs, white papers) with source quality assessment (Information and Software Technology 106, 2019).
GRADE rates certainty of evidence in four levels (Guyatt et al., BMJ 2008;336:995-8).
PICO frames a question as patient, intervention, comparison, outcome (Richardson et al., ACP Journal Club 1995;123:A12-3), reached only through secondary descriptions.
